why: The import is never used in this file.
fix: Delete the import line.

why: A local variable is assigned but never read.
fix: Remove the variable, or use it. If it must stay, rename it with a leading underscore.

why: A private member is declared but never used.
fix: Remove it, or use it.

why: A private field is declared but never read.
fix: Remove it, or use it.

why: This code can never run (it follows a return/throw, or a condition is always false).
fix: Delete the unreachable code, or fix the logic that makes it unreachable.

why: An import points at a file or package that isn't available.
fix: If it's a package, add it (flutter pub add <package>) and run flutter pub get. If it's a file, fix the path or create the file.

why: A value of one type is being assigned to a variable of another type.
fix: Change the variable's type, convert the value (for example int.parse(...)), or cast it if you are certain.

why: The name isn't declared in this scope, or the import that provides it is missing.
fix: Check the spelling, declare it, or add the import that provides it.

why: The class isn't declared or its import is missing.
fix: Import the file that defines it, or fix the class name.

why: That method doesn't exist on this type.
fix: Check for a typo, that the value has the type you expect, or that the extension/mixin providing it is imported.

why: That property doesn't exist on this type.
fix: Check for a typo, that the value has the type you expect, or add the property.

why: An argument's type doesn't match the parameter's type.
fix: Pass a value of the expected type, or convert it first.

why: A required named parameter wasn't passed.
fix: Pass the missing argument.

why: This API is marked deprecated and will be removed.
fix: Switch to the replacement named in the message.

why: print() is flagged in production code because it isn't controllable or filterable.
fix: Use debugPrint, or a logger such as package:logging.

why: The code imports a package that pubspec.yaml doesn't declare.
fix: Add it: flutter pub add <package>.

why: This constructor call can be const, which lets Flutter reuse the object.
fix: Add const.

why: The constructor of an immutable class can be const.
fix: Add const to the constructor.

why: This final variable's value is a compile-time constant.
fix: Change final to const.

why: A parameter is only forwarded to super and can use the shorter super-parameter syntax.
fix: Convert it to a super parameter (Foo({super.key})).

why: A private field is never reassigned.
fix: Make it final.

why: 'this.' isn't needed here.
fix: Remove 'this.'.

why: 'new' is optional in Dart.
fix: Remove 'new'.

why: An overriding member is missing @override.
fix: Add @override.

why: The import path doesn't resolve to a file or an installed package (or its type declarations).
fix: Fix the path or extension. For a package, install it (npm i <package>), plus @types/<package> if it has no types. Check tsconfig 'paths' and 'moduleResolution' if the path is an alias.

why: The name isn't declared or imported in this file.
fix: Import it, declare it, or fix the spelling.

why: The name isn't declared or imported (TypeScript suggests the closest match).
fix: Use the suggested name, or import/declare the one you meant.

why: A value's type doesn't match the type it's assigned to.
fix: Make the value match the declared type, or change the declared type if the value is the one that's right.

why: An argument's type doesn't match the parameter's type.
fix: Pass a value of the parameter's type, or convert it first.

why: The property doesn't exist on that type.
fix: Check for a typo, narrow the type first, or add the property to the type or interface.

why: The call passes a different number of arguments than the function accepts.
fix: Pass the right number of arguments, or update the function's signature.

why: A parameter has no type, so it implicitly has type any (strict mode forbids that).
fix: Add a type annotation to the parameter.

why: The value might be undefined at this point.
fix: Guard it (if (x) ...), use optional chaining (x?.y) or a default (x ?? fallback). Avoid the ! operator unless you are certain.

why: The object might be undefined at this point.
fix: Guard it (if (x) ...), use optional chaining (x?.y) or a default (x ?? fallback).

why: The object might be null at this point.
fix: Guard it (if (x) ...), use optional chaining (x?.y) or a default (x ?? fallback).

why: A variable, parameter or import is declared but never used.
fix: Remove it (or prefix a parameter with an underscore).

why: The identifier isn't defined in this environment.
fix: Import or declare it. If it's a real global (browser or Node), add it to languageOptions.globals (or env in older configs).

why: A variable or import is declared but never used.
fix: Remove it, or use it. Prefix with an underscore only if your config allows that for intentional cases.

why: A variable or import is declared but never used.
fix: Remove it, or use it.

why: An explicit 'any' switches off type checking for that value.
fix: Use a specific type, or unknown and narrow it.

why: A variable is never reassigned.
fix: Use const instead of let.

why: A semicolon is missing or extra, per your style rules.
fix: Fix the semicolon.

why: The quote style doesn't match your style rules.
fix: Use the configured quote style.

why: The indentation doesn't match your style rules.
fix: Re-indent.

why: There's an unnecessary semicolon.
fix: Remove it.

why: A trailing comma is missing or extra, per your style rules.
fix: Fix the trailing comma.

why: A line has trailing whitespace.
fix: Remove it.

why: The file doesn't end with a newline.
fix: Add a final newline.

why: There are too many consecutive blank lines.
fix: Remove the extra blank lines.

why: console.* calls are flagged in this project.
fix: Remove it, or use the project's logger.

why: A value's type doesn't match the type the code expects.
fix: Make the value match the expected type, or convert it (.into(), as, .parse()).

why: The name (value or function) isn't in scope.
fix: Declare it, fix the spelling, or bring it into scope with `use`.

why: A path uses a type, module or crate that isn't in scope or isn't a dependency.
fix: Add the `use` line, or add the crate to Cargo.toml (cargo add <crate>).

why: A `use` path doesn't exist.
fix: Check the path and spelling, and that the crate is in Cargo.toml.

why: The value was moved earlier and can't be used again.
fix: Borrow it (&x), clone it (x.clone()), or restructure who owns the value.

why: That method doesn't exist for this type.
fix: Check for a typo, that the right trait is imported (use Trait), or that the type is what you expect.

why: A variable is declared but never used.
fix: Use it, or prefix the name with an underscore.

why: A `use` line isn't needed.
fix: Remove it.

why: A function or item is never used.
fix: Remove it, use it, or mark it with #[allow(dead_code)] if intentional.

why: A variable is declared but never used (Go treats that as an error).
fix: Remove it, use it, or assign it to _ if that's intentional.

why: An import isn't used (Go treats that as an error).
fix: Remove the import line (goimports -w . does this).

why: The name isn't declared or imported.
fix: Declare it, fix the spelling, or import the package that provides it.

why: Angular can't create something because a service it needs isn't provided here (in this test's TestBed, or in the app config).
fix: Provide it. In a test: TestBed.configureTestingModule({ providers: [TheService] }). For HttpClient use provideHttpClient() and provideHttpClientTesting() (HttpClientTestingModule on older Angular); for Router use provideRouter([]).

pattern: is not a known element|since it isn't a known property
why: A template uses a component, directive or property that Angular doesn't know in this context.
fix: Add the component/directive/module to the imports of the component (standalone) or of TestBed.configureTestingModule, and check the selector spelling.

why: A dependency isn't installed, or an import path is wrong.
fix: Run your package manager's install. If it names a package, add it (npm i <name>; for a tool's missing peer dependency, add that as a devDependency). If it's a relative path, fix it.

pattern: timed out in [0-9]+ ?ms|Exceeded timeout of|Timeout - Async callback
why: The test didn't finish within its time limit, usually an unresolved promise or observable, or a missing await.
fix: Make sure the test awaits or returns its async work, or completes the observable. Raise the timeout only if the work is legitimately slow.

why: Code uses a name that doesn't exist at runtime (typo, missing import, or a browser global such as window/document in a Node test).
fix: Import or declare it. For window/document, run the test in a browser-like environment (jsdom or happy-dom).

why: Code read a property of something that is undefined or null. Usually a value wasn't set up, or a call returned nothing.
fix: Look at the failing line: initialize the value in the test setup, or guard it (x?.y).

why: Something that isn't a function was called (wrong import, missing mock, or undefined).
fix: Check what the name really holds at that point: the import, the mock, or a typo.

why: The output no longer matches the stored snapshot.
fix: If the change is intended, update the snapshots (your test runner's -u flag). Otherwise fix the code that changed the output.

pattern: (Expected|expected).*(Actual|Received|to be|to equal|to deeply equal|to have|to contain)|Which: is different
why: The code under test produced something different from what the test expects.
fix: Compare Expected with Actual above. If the code's behavior is wrong, fix the code; if the expectation is outdated, update the test.
